proposed_from.topic:
When does plan turnover still permit a finite nonparametric upper bound on switching costs? A sharp iid frontier for short health-choice panels. Observe n independent consumers in one known design cell: (Y0,Y1,Y2), fixed initial choice Y0=h0, two observed nonempty menus M1,M2 contained in a universe D={1,...,J}, J finite, and known finite rational prices p_td for d in Mt. Initial h0 belongs to D and may be absent from M1. Utility is -p_td + κ 1{d=Y(t-1)} + λ_d + ε_td, κ≥0 common. Conditional on λ, ε1 and ε2 are iid, have an absolutely continuous distribution on R^J with arbitrary within-period dependence; the mixing law of λ and the conditional shock law are unrestricted. Choices maximize utility, uniquely almost surely. Let P=(P_ab:a∈M1,b∈M2) be the observed path table; assume at least one κ/model rationalizes P. Θ(P) contains every κ≥0 with an exact rationalization; U(P)=sup Θ(P), taking value +∞ if unbounded. Multiple observed cells with arbitrary cell-specific heterogeneity can subsequently be intersected; that is not needed in the kernel.

Precise answer-open theorem problem. For every finite rational design above, construct from its utility-comparison graph a finite price threshold K and an explicit compact terminal path-probability body C∞ such that the exact compatible body Cκ equals C∞ for all κ>K, and prove sharpness in both directions by constructing iid random-utility rationalizations. Derive an observable necessary-and-sufficient criterion for U(P)<∞, expressed using this constructed body rather than a quantifier over structural distributions, and recover the exact U(P) by a finite price-breakpoint search with certified feasibility. Mandatory non-generic core: for J=3, h0∈M1, and every pure-entry or pure-exit menu pair {a,b}↔{a,b,c}, derive a complete explicit analytic characterization of C∞ (a finite Boolean combination of inequalities in the six entries P_ab, with no latent variables, optimization, or unevaluated quantifier elimination), including boundary cases and constructive attainability. Do not presume that corrected Jensen inequalities are complete. Extend computation to any finite J via a certified inner/outer approximation with a proved deterministic error bound. Pair with a confidence set for Θ(P) that covers the entire set with probability at least 1-α uniformly over the stated model and preserves +∞ when the terminal body cannot be rejected. Exact formulas/inequality lists are the theorem’s output, not assumed hypotheses.

Computation and inference: At fixed κ, enumerate deterministic response tables f: one first-period choice and a second-period choice for each a∈M1. Retain f iff one shock vector z satisfies all strict utility inequalities simultaneously; solve this difference-constraint feasibility problem with cycle tests. For probabilities q on retained tables define v_ab(q)=(sum_f q_f 1{f1=a})(sum_g q_g 1{g2(a)=b}). The known iid mixture gives Cκ=conv{v(q):q in simplex}; prove attainability with continuous shocks inside open patches. At T=2 this is a linear image of normalized completely-positive matrices E[qq′]. That observation is only a computation starting point. Enumerate price breakpoints where response-table feasibility changes; terminal graph is after the last breakpoint. A rational simplex grid plus convex hull LP gives inner approximations; the quadratic map’s Lipschitz bound gives a certified outer inflation, with refinement until a requested positive precision is reached. The J=3 analytic elimination and sharpness are mandatory; a black-box copositive/QE call alone fails the contract. Estimate all m=|M1||M2| path probabilities by multinomial frequencies. Invert certified distance-to-Cκ tests using a simultaneous multinomial concentration region, including optimization error. For example a sup-norm Hoeffding box radius sqrt(log(2m/α)/(2n)) supplies a finite-sample starting point; certify uniform whole-set coverage and consistent finite-upper-bound declaration whenever D∞(P)>0. No uniform consistency at D∞=0 is claimed. This rung is supporting, not the novelty: Tamer–Walker 2608.25814 already studies general PMF-to-identified-set Bayesian inference.

Grounding and exclusions: Theorem 2.3(a) proves P(Y1∈A,Y2∈A)≥P(Y1∈A)^2 under structural-utility dominance and a common menu. Its load-bearing samplewise containment fails with entrants; conditioning on selecting continuing plans does not restore the latent mixture. Appendix proof, pp.50–52, makes this failure explicit. The supplied paper pp.20–21 excludes changing menus and loses year-pairs crossing 2011; p.40 leaves the nonparametric varying-menu problem open. Closest: Mbakop (2023), arXiv:2305.15691, https://arxiv.org/html/2305.15691v1 — Prop.2.14 gives nonpolyhedral iid bodies; Example3.5/Thm3.6 compute sharp stationarity inequalities; Remark3.9 and footnote50 show the health assumption is iid-equivalent, already represent its CCPs as mixtures of products, and show his inequalities complement the Pakes inequalities. Difference: an explicit complete turnover upper-tail frontier and analytic three-plan iid body, not generic sharp-set computation. Generic PMF/set Bayesian inference is closed-by:Tamer–Walker 2608.25814 (Aug2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25814. Live exact-pair and citing searches on Sept7,2026 found no result resolving this turnover/conditional-iid frontier; absence from bounded searches is not proof of novelty. Author research pages and NBER still point to June/July2025 paper; SSRN metadata reports Apr23,2026 revision, and a second author-hosted PDF returned HTTP403, so a full independent later-revision comparison remains a presolve check. Internal collision_snapshot.json was checked only for dedup: no health, menu, Pakes, Mbakop, multinomial, or relevant switching-cost title; no failed/downgraded run contents were read.

Consumer: Pakes et al.’s published NBER working paper 29025, health-plan application §§3,5: it drops observations experiencing plan entry/exit, and cannot use year-pairs crossing 2011 because too few menus remain stable. The result permits using those observed menu-change comparisons while retaining flexible fixed effects and iid nonparametric disturbances, and states exactly when a finite switching-cost ceiling survives. A journal-published additional consumer is Polyakova (2016), AEJ:Applied 8(3),165–195, Regulation of Insurance with Adverse Selection and Switching Costs: Evidence from Medicare Part D, DOI 10.1257/app.20150004: structural estimates of inertia feed risk-sorting and regulation counterfactuals. It could use the resulting nonparametric ceiling as a robustness restriction on switching-cost magnitudes in stable-quality menu-turnover cells; the theorem does not itself identify welfare or validate cells with changed plan quality.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derived strict-cycle feasibility, continuous-shock convexification, finite rational price-breakpoint saturation, and the equivalence between a finite switching-cost ceiling and positive distance from the terminal probability body. It obtained an explicit analytic entry body for one relative-price sign and two informative boundary faces. A legal all-positive entry table has an exact upper endpoint of four, passes the corrected Jensen inequality, and admits a terminal exchangeability rationalization while violating the iid terminal restriction. Exact rational reconstruction, terminal separating inequalities, strict patch margins, and numerical analytic-body checks were reproduced. Checks included all nine terminal response classes, zero probabilities, unattained endpoints, initial-plan exit, and singleton menus. Current primary comparisons found no affirmative collision; the April 2026 SSRN revision remains inaccessible and requires retrieval and comparison.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete the constructive latent-free analytic projection for negative entry with both off-diagonal probabilities positive, zero-sign entry, and all six exit classes, including every boundary case and attaining mixture.
EARLY KILL TEST: Derive the negative-entry allocation formula and compare its support values with exact quadratic optimization over all twenty response-pair curves. A discrepancy kills that formula; inability to complete the analytic elimination requires reassessing the field-tier scope.

proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest result, Pakes et al. Theorem 2.3(a) on PDF p. 20 of the canonical revised-July-2025 manuscript, derives its adjacent-period common-menu joint probability inequality from Condition 2.2 with the two comparator subsets equal in one common choice universe. The associated samplewise containment does not encode the full winner--loser comparisons after entry or exit, and their application therefore drops changing-offering comparisons. Mbakop's Proposition 2.14 and Remark 3.9 show why merely adding linear inequalities is insufficient under conditional iid, but stop at a generic support-function representation. The proposed advance is the design-specific theorem object \(\mathcal C_\infty\): a finite terminal response graph, an iff observable finite-ceiling criterion, exact breakpoint recovery, and a complete analytic projection for all three-plan pure-entry and pure-exit classes with boundary attainability. The last component is not a relabeling of generic sharp-set computation and is the decisive novelty gate.

S5: Proof-producing singularity-robust certifier for arbitrary finite menus
S6: Necessary-and-sufficient multi-cell point-identification certificate for a common switching cost
S7: Local minimax testing theory at smooth, corner, and self-contact strata of the terminal body
S8: Pure-entry and pure-exit design taxonomy for universal upper-tail informativeness

seed_details.red_team: Immediate from nesting because iid is stronger than exchangeability, which is stronger than stationarity.
seed_details.rebuttal: Set nesting orders endpoints but does not characterize equality or produce a nondegenerate observable region in which only the product restriction makes the ceiling finite.

seed_details.kernel: Under a primitive radius \(\delta\) for time variation in person-by-plan utility, derive sharp \(U(P,\delta)\) and the critical \(\delta^*\) at which a finite ceiling becomes infinite.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Fixed effects no longer cancel across dates; augment each graph edge by bounded drift and derive the critical drift from robust cycle weights before applying iid convexification.
